text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,349.65, down 1.75% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 slipped 1.41%. The sell‑off was wide‑based – only 133 stocks advanced against 360 decliners, giving a breadth score of 62.2 (rated “HEALTHY”). Bank Nifty fell harder at –3.17% to 62,585.35. Both indices are trading just above their 20‑day moving average (around 63 % of stocks above it) but below the 200‑day level (≈24,000 for Nifty).  

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹5,672.99 crore, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹2,760.12 crore, extending an 18‑day buying streak for FIIs and a 4‑day selling streak for DIIs. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.74 for Nifty and 0.71 for Bank Nifty, indicating slightly more call interest. Max‑pain levels sit at 25,350 (Nifty) and 62,500 (Bank Nifty), with support walls around 25,300–25,400 and 62,500–62,600 respectively.  

Watch the 25,562 P pivot and the 25,131 S1 support on Nifty, and the 63,441 P and 61,690 S1 on Bank Nifty for the next session. Key headlines to monitor include RBI’s stance on pension‑money equity inflows and any fresh US rate or geopolitical news that could move the India VIX, which is up 2.19% at 17.7. Keep an eye on sector rotation – PSU banks and realty remain leading, while IT and oil‑gas are lagging.
